USPS shows delay; need to set expectations and outline next steps (wait window, contacting USPS, then seller). No tools apply (shipment tool exists but we already have equivalent info from user). Be concise, give clear thresholds and what I can do further. </think>
<plan>
1. Explain what “In transit, arriving late” usually means and typical delay window.

3. Offer to help draft a message to the seller or organize details if needed.
</plan>
<action type="say">
“In transit, arriving late” from USPS usually means the package is still moving but missed its projected milestone or got held at a processing center. It often resolves on its own in a few days.

Given it’s been stuck with that message for 3 days to Birmingham 35205:

1) Timing / when to worry  
- If it’s still “In transit, arriving late” but less than 7 days past the original ETA, USPS will usually still ask you to wait.  
- If it gets to about 7+ days past the ETA with no scans, it’s worth escalating.

2) What you can do right now  
- On the USPS tracking page, use “Text & Email Updates” so you don’t have to keep checking.  
- If you have (or can create) a USPS account, you can also file a “Help Request” or “Service Request” directly from the tracking page; that pings your local post office to look for it.

3) If it doesn’t move soon  
- If there’s no new scan within the next 2–3 days, I’d:  
  • Take a screenshot or copy of the tracking page, and  
  • Contact the seller with: your order ID (ODR-105234), tracking number (94001118992234567890), and the fact it’s shown “In transit, arriving late” since [date it first appeared].  
- Ask them to either:  
  • Initiate a trace with USPS, or  
  • Reship/refund if it’s declared lost.

If you’d like, paste the exact tracking history (or the date it first showed “arriving late”) and I can tell you whether it looks more like a normal delay or something that’s likely lost, and I can draft a message you can send to the seed company.</action>
